title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to provide your body with sufficient iron and folate. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of your baby. However, choosing iron- and folate-rich foods can be challenging. Here are three recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, making it easy for expectant mothers to supplement their diet.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Broccoli Bowl
* 100g grilled chicken (heme iron)
* 100g broccoli (vitamin C)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper to taste

Grilled chicken is an excellent source of heme iron, while broccoli is rich in vitamin C, which enhances iron absorption. Grill the chicken for 20 minutes, then mix with broccoli and cooked white rice.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry
* 100g beef stir-fry (heme iron)
* 100g bell pepper (vitamin C)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper to taste

Beef stir-fry is a rich source of heme iron, while bell pepper is high in vitamin C, which boosts iron absorption. Stir-fry the beef for 15 minutes, then mix with bell pepper and cooked white rice.

## Recipe 3: Black Bean and Tomato Bowl
* 100g cooked black beans (non-heme iron)
* 100g tomato (vitamin C)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper to taste

Black beans are an excellent source of non-heme iron, while tomatoes are rich in vitamin C, which enhances iron absorption. Cook the black beans for 20 minutes, then mix with tomatoes and cooked white rice.

## Food Safety Notes
When pregnant, it's crucial to prioritize food safety to avoid bacterial infections and other health issues. Ensure that all foods are cooked thoroughly and hot before consumption. Additionally, avoid eating raw or undercooked foods, such as sushi or salads.

## Conclusion
These three recipes make it easy for expectant mothers to supplement their diet with iron and folate. Remember that choosing nutrient-dense and safe foods is vital during pregnancy.
